What is claimed is:

1. A charging control system for a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch, the system comprising:

a plurality of connector stations, each connector station of the plurality comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective electric-vehicle connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current of the respective electric-vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:

subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and

verify a resulting connector current of that connector station with the connector current sensor of that connector station; and

wherein the controller is further configured to send a reduced pilot command through the control-pilot interface of at least one connector station of the plurality and to start a verification interval, and, when a measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors of the plurality of connector stations one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

2. input.summary: The complete filing candidate is in place: title, cross-reference and government-support sections each reading Not applicable., field, background, summary, brief description of the four drawings, detailed description, claims 1 to 16, abstract at 142 words, the 23-entry numeral table, and four figure briefs. This turn adds two claims and changes nothing else. Claim 15 makes the system re-evaluate the measured branch current between successive openings of the contactors in the stored shedding order and open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch limit, and claim 16 is the method counterpart. Both use the words already in the detailed description passage on the shedding order, so the support is verbatim and no description text had to be widened. They give the ladder a fallback between the whole shedding sequence of claim 1 and the recovery and fault claims that follow: the closed-loop character of the shedding itself, opening only as many contactors as the measurement shows are needed. On the rest of the gate, everything checkable against files passes. Every numeral in draft/numerals.md is used in the detailed description and every numeral used there is in the table, each against one part name. Each brief's geometry uses only the numerals that brief lists, no numeral appears on two sheets, and the four lists partition the table exactly: FIG. 1 with 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114; FIG. 2 with 102, 106, 110, 120, 122, 124, 126; FIG. 3 with 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 132, 134, 136; FIG. 4 with 200 through 214. Sheet numbering agrees across draft/07-drawings.md, the file names, the brief headings and the detailed description. No sheet carries more than eight numerals, the briefs measure 2712, 2798, 2791 and 2586 characters, no sectional view is specified so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed, and no placeholder, note, question or em dash appears in draft/ or figures/. The blockers that remain are the rendered sheets and review/figure-audit-evidence.json. Producing image files is outside what I can do here, so the numeral-in-drawing gate, the sheet-per-figure gate and the pixel, OCR, leader and geometry checks close when the drawing pass renders these four briefs and binds the evidence. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The two new claims fill a real gap in the ladder. Claim 1 requires opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit, which an opponent could read as merely sequencing the openings. Claims 15 and 16 recite the measurement step that sits between the openings and the stopping rule that follows from it, so the shedding is itself closed on the branch measurement rather than being a fixed sequence run to completion. That is a feature worth arguing on its own, which is the test for whether a dependent claim earns its place.

I took the wording straight from the detailed description sentence stating that the contactors are opened one at a time with the measured branch current re-evaluated between openings and that no further contactor is opened once it is below the branch limit. Using the description's own words keeps antecedent basis clean, since claim 1 and claim 9 each introduce a measured branch current and then refer to the measured branch current, and it avoids widening the description to support a claim.

I appended rather than renumbered. Inserting the new fallback next to claim 1 would have shifted every dependent number and broken the references the reviewer has already traced through claims 2 to 14, for no gain in scope.

Nothing else changed. The reviewer states the prose and the briefs are sound and that no specification change is required once sheets exist, so any further edit would be churn against text verified clean over several cycles, and edits to briefs specifically risk reopening the leader endpoint and character-limit issues that are now closed.

I did not simplify or strip the briefs to make a render finish faster. The isolation strokes, the separate unqualified line from the first connector current sensor 122, and the return path from the ordered contactor shedding step 210 each carry disclosed content, and trading them for a gate result would let the pipeline dictate the invention.

No third statutory class was added. A medium claim would need instructions stored for execution, and the disclosure describes stored values, a signed token and a last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory but never a stored program, so that claim would rest on something the inventor did not say.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. New claims 15 and 16 deepen that theme by making the shedding itself measurement-driven, stopping as soon as the branch measurement permits rather than running a fixed sequence, which is a narrower position to fall back to if the ordered shedding of claim 1 is met by something in art later found. The rest of the ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

Claim 15 makes the system re-evaluate the measured branch current between successive openings of the contactors in the stored shedding order and open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch limit, and claim 16 is the method counterpart. Both use the words already in the detailed description passage on the shedding order, so the support is verbatim and no description text had to be widened. They give the ladder a fallback between the whole shedding sequence of claim 1 and the recovery and fault claims that follow: the closed-loop character of the shedding itself, opening only as many contactors as the measurement shows are needed. On the rest of the gate, everything checkable against files passes. Claims 15 and 16 recite the measurement step that sits between the openings and the stopping rule that follows from it, so the shedding is itself closed on the branch measurement rather than being a fixed sequence run to completion. That is a feature worth arguing on its own, which is the test for whether a dependent claim earns its place.

I took the wording straight from the detailed description sentence stating that the contactors are opened one at a time with the measured branch current re-evaluated between openings and that no further contactor is opened once it is below the branch limit. Using the description's own words keeps antecedent basis clean, since claim 1 and claim 9 each introduce a measured branch current and then refer to the measured branch current, and it avoids widening the description to support a claim.

Nothing else changed. 1	What is claimed is:
2	
3	1. A charging control system for a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch, the system comprising:
4	
5	a plurality of connector stations, each connector station of the plurality comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective electric-vehicle connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current of the respective electric-vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector;
6	
7	a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;
8	
9	an isolated local bus; and
10	
11	a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;
12	
13	wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:
14	
15	subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;
16	
17	assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;
18	
19	send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and
20

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:

subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and

verify a resulting connector current of that connector station with the connector current sensor of that connector station; and

View: schematic block diagram of the charging control system, in plain line work. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins. No text is drawn by the geometry; numerals are applied afterward.

Geometry:

- A horizontal line spans the upper third of the drawing area. This line is the branch conductor 102.
- A small open rectangle straddles the branch conductor 102 near its left end, the line passing through it and continuing right. This rectangle is the branch current sensor 104, shown schematically.
- Three vertical drop lines descend from the branch conductor 102 to the right of the branch current sensor 104, each ending at the top edge of one of three plain rectangles standing side by side in the middle band of the drawing area.
- The leftmost of the three rectangles is the first connector station 110, the middle rectangle is the second connector station 112, and the rightmost rectangle is the non-charging load 114, all shown schematically.
- A larger plain rectangle stands in the lower left of the drawing area, below and left of the first connector station 110. This rectangle is the edge controller 100, shown schematically.
- A horizontal line runs from the right side of the edge controller 100 across the lower band of the drawing area, with two vertical branches rising from it to the bottom edges of the first connector station 110 and the second connector station 112. This line is the isolated local bus 106. Two short parallel strokes cross it between the edge controller 100 and the left branch, indicating isolation schematically.

For the branch conductor 102, end the leader on that line clear of any junction and of the small open rectangle straddling it. input.summary: Both verified defects are fixed. FIG. 1 now draws the connector-current-sensor coupling that the specification asserts and that FIG. 2 already showed: a separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100, and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106, and the brief states that these lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100. No numeral was added, the numeral list and the endpoint paragraph are unchanged, and the two system views now agree with each other and with the description paragraph that limits the bus to assigned current limits, contactor commands and control-pilot status. Adding that line work took the brief past the 2800-character ceiling, so I recovered the space by tightening wording only, and FIG. 1 stands at 2798 characters with every body, path and schematic marking intact, including the isolation strokes and the branch current sensor coupling. Second, the claims are regrouped so that the system claims run 1 to 9 and the method claims run 10 to 16. The re-evaluation-between-openings system claim now sits at 9, immediately after the other claims depending from claim 1, and the method independent claim moves to 10 with its dependents renumbered 11 to 16. Only claim numbers and dependency references changed; not one word of claim text was altered, and every dependency now points backward to the correct claim, with claim 14 depending from claim 13 as before and claims 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 depending from method claim 10. The description, the numeral table, the drawing descriptions, draft/numerals.md and the FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 briefs are untouched. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 per sheet, every brief inside the character limit at 2798, 2798, 2791 and 2586, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. Nothing in draft/ or figures/ carries a placeholder, note or question. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The FIG. 1 defect was a real inconsistency and the fix belonged in the drawing, not the text. The description says the bus carries limits, contactor commands and pilot status, and separately that each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller and reports its measurement, which is supported by the disclosure sentence requiring the controller to verify the resulting connector current with the corresponding sensor. FIG. 2 already drew that separate path, so the system view was the file that was wrong. Adding the two lines to FIG. 1 brings the views into agreement without touching the specification, which is the correct direction given that text outranks figures.

I added the coupling without a numeral. The lines are the couplings of parts that already carry numerals, and inventing a numeral for a connection would have forced an entry in the numeral table and a place on a sheet for something the disclosure never names as a part.

The brief describes those lines as clear of the isolated local bus 106 because that separation is the point the description makes: the sensor measurement does not ride the bus. That is a positive relationship statement, not a negative linework control, and it is the minimum needed to keep the drawn geometry faithful to the paragraph it illustrates.

Character budget again came out of wording rather than content. Every disclosed element of FIG. 1 survived: the branch conductor with the branch current sensor straddling it, three drops to the two connector stations and the non-charging load, the bus with its two branches and the isolation strokes, the sensor-to-controller line, and the network interface.

On the claims I took the regrouping route rather than leaving a system claim stranded after the method group. Moving the re-evaluation claim to 9 puts every claim depending from claim 1 together and every claim depending from the method independent together, which is what the grouping requirement asks for, and renumbering is the only change that achieves it without rewriting scope.

I checked every dependency after renumbering rather than trusting the shift: claims 2 to 9 refer to claim 1, claim 4 to claim 3, claims 6 and 7 to claim 5, claims 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 to claim 10, and claim 14 to claim 13. All references point to earlier claims, and the antecedent for the measured branch current in claims 9 and 16 comes from claim 1 and claim 10 respectively.

figures/FIG-1.md: tightened wording throughout so the brief holds at 2798 characters, with the numeral list, the endpoint paragraph and all existing geometry unchanged.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. Nothing in claim scope changed this turn; the claims were regrouped and renumbered only. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating the branch current between successive openings and stopping as soon as it is below the limit. The remainder of the ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

input.summary: One file changed. figures/FIG-3.md placed the isolation marking on the isolated local bus 106 outside the enclosing rectangle of the edge controller 100 and then allowed the leader for 106 to end anywhere to the right of that rectangle, which is the same stretch the two short parallel strokes cross, so the leader could have terminated on the marking and read as identifying it rather than the bus. The endpoint sentence now reads that the leader ends on that line at a point whose horizontal position lies to the right of the right side of the enclosing rectangle and clear of the two short parallel strokes crossing that line, which matches the instruction the FIG. 1 brief already carries for the same numeral over the same kind of geometry, so the two briefs now specify one endpoint rule for numeral 106. The added clause took the brief over the 2800-character ceiling, so I recovered the space in the same file by tightening wording only: the branch conductor bullet now says the line passes through the small open rectangle and continues right rather than repeating the numeral, the sensor-to-controller line refers back to that sensor instead of naming it again, and the network interface sentence folds its outgoing stub into the same sentence. FIG. 3 stands at 2791 characters, still lists 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 132, 134 and 136, and every body, line, junction and the isolation marking is unchanged. No geometry bullet lost a relationship, no numeral moved, and the isolation strokes stay because they carry the disclosed fact that the bus is isolated between the controller and the connector stations. Nothing else in the workspace was touched: the claims, now the system group 1 to 9 and the method group 10 to 16, the detailed description, the drawing descriptions, draft/numerals.md, and the FIG. 1, FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 per sheet, briefs at 2798, 2798, 2791 and 2586 characters, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. reasoning: This was a genuine ambiguity between two briefs for one numeral, and the FIG. 3 version was the loose one. On both sheets the isolated local bus 106 carries a schematic isolation marking, and on FIG. 1 the endpoint instruction already steered the leader away from it. Bringing FIG. 3 into line means the same numeral is placed by the same rule wherever it appears, which is what keeps a reader from having to guess whether a leader points at the bus or at the marking on it.

I fixed the endpoint wording rather than moving the isolation strokes or shortening the bus. The strokes depict the disclosed isolation between the controller and the connector stations, and relocating drawing content to make room for a label would trade disclosed substance for label convenience.

The target stays broad. Any point on the run of the bus to the right of the rectangle qualifies except the short span occupied by the strokes, so there is no midpoint, fraction or distance in the instruction, and the one exclusion exists to distinguish two things that sit on the same line rather than to control appearance.

Character budget came out of repetition, not content: a numeral repeated within a sentence that had already named its part, a sensor named twice in consecutive clauses, and a separate sentence for a short stub line. Every body, path, junction and schematic marking on the sheet survived intact.

I left the other three briefs and all of draft/ alone. The review reports the source ledger closed, the claim grouping cured, and those briefs consistent, so any further edit would be churn against text that is verified clean, and edits to briefs specifically risk reopening endpoint or character-limit issues that are now closed.

This turn changed one leader-endpoint sentence and some wording in a single figure brief; no claim, description passage or numeral changed, so the shape of the case stands as filed. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating the branch current between successive openings and stopping as soon as it falls below the limit. The remainder of the ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

input.summary: Two geometry bullets are deleted and nothing else changed. figures/FIG-1.md no longer draws lines running from the bottom edges of the first connector station 110 and the second connector station 112 to the edge controller 100 clear of the isolated local bus 106, and figures/FIG-2.md no longer draws a line running downward from the first connector current sensor 122 and out of the enclosing rectangle. Those two bullets together asserted a second controller-to-station signalling path dedicated to connector-current reporting and placed outside the isolated local bus, which is topology with technical substance that the sources do not state. The disclosed coupling itself is untouched: draft/08-detailed-description.md still says each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it, and it still limits the bus to assigned current limits, contactor commands and control-pilot status. No replacement path was drawn and the sensor output was not re-routed onto the isolated local bus 106, since neither routing is disclosed and a block diagram need not depict the reporting channel. The deletions orphan nothing. FIG. 1 still carries 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112 and 114 in its geometry and list, FIG. 2 still carries 102, 106, 110, 120, 122, 124 and 126 with the first connector current sensor 122 still straddling the power path beside the first contactor 120, and both leader-endpoint paragraphs are unchanged, as is draft/numerals.md. The briefs now measure 2505, 2590, 2791 and 2586 characters, all within the ceiling, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 numerals per sheet, all 23 numerals defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. Claims 1 to 9 in the system group and 10 to 16 in the method group, the detailed description, the drawing descriptions and the FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 briefs are untouched, and nothing in draft/ or figures/ carries a placeholder, note or question. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: Deleting was the right repair rather than relabelling, because the problem was not how the line was described but that it existed at all. A drawn channel that bypasses the isolation boundary tells a reader the measurement reaches the controller outside the isolated bus, and the sources name only two things on the one disclosed controller-to-station path. Keeping the line and softening its caption would have left the same assertion in the pixels.

I did not move the sensor output onto the isolated local bus 106 as a substitute. That routing is equally undisclosed, and it is the assertion an earlier cycle already removed from the description. Leaving the reporting channel undepicted keeps both views silent on a question the inventor did not answer, which is the only position the sources support.

The description sentence stays because it is supported at a different level of generality: the disclosure requires the controller to verify the resulting connector current with the corresponding sensor, so a coupling exists, but the path it takes is not stated. Text can say coupled without saying how; a line on a block diagram cannot.

The deletions also close the cross-view gap the finding identified. FIG. 3 is the enlarged view of the same edge controller 100 and showed no connector-current input, so removing the two inputs that FIG. 1 drew arriving at that block leaves the three views consistent with one another without adding anything to FIG. 3.

Nothing was rewritten to fill the space the bullets left. Both briefs read coherently as they stand, every remaining body and path is disclosed, and the shorter files simply sit further under the character ceiling, so there was no reason to add compensating prose.
changes: figures/FIG-1.md: deleted the geometry bullet describing a separate line from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100 and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106 and reporting each station's measured connector current.
figures/FIG-2.md: deleted the geometry bullet describing a separate line running downward from the first connector current sensor 122 and out through the lower side of the enclosing rectangle.
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. This turn removed two lines from two figure briefs; no claim, description passage or numeral changed, so the shape of the case stands as filed. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. Claim 1 requires the verification to happen at the connector current sensor without dictating the path by which the measurement reaches the controller, so removing the drawn path costs no claim support. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem the combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating branch current between successive openings and stopping once it is below the limit, and the remaining ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

In the following description, reference is made to the accompanying drawings, which form a part of this disclosure and show particular embodiments by way of illustration. Other embodiments may be used and structural or logical changes may be made without departing from the scope of the disclosure. Like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views.

Overview of the system

FIG. 1 shows a charging control system in which an edge controller 100 manages charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the plurality of connectors. The allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, referred to in this description as the branch limit, is lower than the sum of the ratings of the connectors that the branch conductor 102 supplies. The branch limit is a stored value that corresponds to the aggregate current the branch is permitted to carry.

The branch conductor 102 supplies a first connector station 110 and a second connector station 112. Two connector stations are shown for clarity of illustration. The system accommodates a larger plurality of connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each further connector station of the plurality. The branch conductor 102 also supplies a non-charging load 114, which is load on the same branch other than the connector stations.

A branch current sensor 104 is located upstream of the contactors of the connector stations and measures the total current on the branch conductor 102. The branch current sensor 104 is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured branch current to it.

The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106. The isolated local bus 106 carries assigned current limits and contactor commands from the edge controller 100 to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors of the connector stations, and carries control-pilot status from the connector stations to the edge controller 100. Each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it. The isolated local bus 106 is isolated between the edge controller 100 and the connector stations.

A network interface 108 connects the edge controller 100 to a remote management system. As described below, the network interface 108 conveys remote schedules and authorizations to the edge controller 100 and conveys uploaded meter records from the edge controller 100, but the safety behaviour of the system does not depend on the availability of the network interface 108.

The connector station

FIG. 2 shows the first connector station 110 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The first connector station 110 comprises a first contactor 120, a first connector current sensor 122, a first control-pilot interface 124, and a first electric-vehicle connector 126. The first contactor 120 is connected in the power path between the branch conductor 102 and the first electric-vehicle connector 126 and, when closed, permits current to flow from the branch conductor 102 to a vehicle coupled to the first electric-vehicle connector 126. The first connector current sensor 122 measures the connector current flowing in that power path, that is, the current actually drawn by the vehicle coupled to the first electric-vehicle connector 126.

The first control-pilot interface 124 presents a control-pilot signal to the vehicle coupled to the first electric-vehicle connector 126. The control-pilot signal advertises a maximum current, called here the assigned limit, that the vehicle is permitted to draw, and the first control-pilot interface 124 reports whether a vehicle is connected. The first control-pilot interface 124 therefore serves both as the command path by which an assigned limit reaches the vehicle and as a status path by which the presence of a connected vehicle is reported to the edge controller 100.

Each connector station of the plurality further has a local connector identifier. The local connector identifier is a stored value that distinguishes one connector of the plurality from another.

input.summary: Both findings are fixed. FIG. 2's isolated local bus 106 now branches inside the enclosing rectangle to the first control-pilot interface 124, to the first contactor 120, and to the first connector current sensor 122, so the sheet shows how the measurement the description asserts and claim 1 requires reaches the controller. Paragraph 11 of the detailed description matches that in its own terms: the bus carries assigned current limits and contactor commands out to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors, carries control-pilot status and measured connector current back, and each connector current sensor is coupled over the isolated local bus 106 to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it. Because the bus is the only controller-to-station link on FIG. 1, the three views now agree without any change to FIG. 1 or FIG. 3. Second, the untraced clause about the local fault indicator 134 operating independently of the network interface 108 is gone; the sentence now reads that the indicator provides an indication at the equipment itself, which is a gloss on the disclosed word local. Nothing was substituted for the removed clause, and the traced statement in paragraph 13 that the safety behaviour of the system does not depend on the availability of the network interface 108 still stands where it belongs. No claim changed. Claim 4 and claim 12 already recite the local fault indicator with no network-independence limitation, and claim 1 requires verification at the connector current sensor without dictating the medium, so both fixes leave scope untouched. draft/numerals.md, the drawing descriptions, the per-sheet numeral lists and the FIG. 1, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 briefs are unchanged. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 per sheet, the briefs measure 2505, 2637, 2791 and 2586 characters, no sectional view exists so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed, and nothing in draft/ or figures/ carries a placeholder, note or question. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The gap was real and had to close on the drawing side plus a matching sentence, not by weakening the claim. Claim 1 requires the controller to verify the resulting connector current at that connector's sensor, so the measurement path is a claimed feature and a drawing set that shows the sensor touching nothing but the power path leaves that feature undepicted. Putting the sensor on the disclosed bus uses the one controller-to-station medium the sources name and the only such link drawn on FIG. 1, so it adds no channel the disclosure does not have.

I amended paragraph 11 in the same move so the text and the sheet describe one architecture. Leaving the description saying the sensor is coupled by some unnamed route while FIG. 2 drew it on the bus would have swapped one cross-file inconsistency for another.
